predecessors.name: Hittite Empire
predecessors.text: Gurgum round Marqas (Kahramanmaras); the page gives no extent, so the modern province (13,400 km2, 36.3-37.7 E, 37.4-38.5 N) is the researcher's reading

successors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
successors.text: Gurgum round Marqas (Kahramanmaras); the page gives no extent, so the modern province (13,400 km2, 36.3-37.7 E, 37.4-38.5 N) is the researcher's reading

ledger.x: c. 950 BC: Gurgum's first recorded event. 'Its first recorded event is the reign of Larama I, c. 950 BC'; the infobox says 'Established: Unknown' and the king table lists Astuwaramanza in the late 11th century, so the start is the page's first dated year, not a founding.
858 BC: Muwatalli II submits to Assyria.
743 BC: Tarhulara joins the anti-Assyrian alliance.

wars.name: Halparuntiya III's invasion of Kummuh
wars.outcome: Halparuntiya III 'invaded Kummuh in 805 BC, and Assyria fixed the border'; he also joined a coalition against Zakkur of Hamath c.

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III against the Urartu-Arpad alliance
wars.outcome: Tiglath-Pileser III defeated the alliance, invaded Gurgum and destroyed 100 Gurgumaean cities; Tarhulara stayed on the throne as a tributary.

wars.name: Sargon II's annexation of Gurgum
wars.outcome: Muwatalli III killed Tarhulara; Sargon II deposed him, deported him and annexed Gurgum.

certainty.note: The page gives no extent; the shape is the modern province round Marqas.
